selectedDefects.issueTitle: Double-clicking with mouse button 4-5 quickly acts like double-clicking with LMB
selectedDefects.pullRequestTitle: Fix mouse side-button double-click triggering left-button behavior

frameworkVerified.evidence: three Avalonia package references in the shared project; the Windows head is OutputType>WinExe on net11.0-windows10.0.22621.0

selectedDefects.whySuitable: Avalonia routes raw pointer events through its own input pipeline before any automation peer sees them, and this defect lives exactly there: a double click made with pointer button 4 or 5 is classified as a left-button double click and runs the left-button action (window state change) instead of the side-button action. The adapter must locate the image surface in the Windows UI Automation tree that Avalonia projects, synthesise a side-button double click over its bounding rectangle, and then read back which action ran from the same tree. That is a full round trip through the Avalonia-to-UIA bridge rather than an internal Avalonia assertion
remaining: confirm the Avalonia UIA bridge exposes the main window content with a stable automation id at these revisions, since Avalonia's automation peers are sparser than WPF's
confirm the .NET 11 SDK is installable in the guest
define the observable that distinguishes the left-button action from the side-button action through automation properties rather than pixels
build both revisions in the native x86_64 Windows VM

selectedDefects.pullRequestTitle: Fix Ctrl+S triggering image rotation instead of save

frameworkVerified.evidence: three Avalonia package references in the shared project; the Windows head is OutputType>WinExe on net11.0-windows10.0.22621.0

selectedDefects.whySuitable: a modifier-key gesture is mismatched in Avalonia's key-binding table, so Ctrl+S rotates the displayed image instead of opening the save flow. The trigger is a key chord delivered to a focused Avalonia window and the observable is which of two windows or which image orientation the automation tree reports afterwards, so it exercises the adapter's keyboard action path and its tree observation in one step. It is also a different input class from the pointer defect above, which keeps the two PicView candidates from collapsing into one identity
remaining: read the diff of MainKeyboardShortcuts.cs on the VM and pin the exact observable, since the issue is written in Chinese and the title carries no detail
confirm the save dialog is an in-process Avalonia window rather than the Win32 common dialog, otherwise the observation leaves the target's tree
build both revisions in the native x86_64 Windows VM

selectedDefects.issueTitle: Cannot casually hover the mouse over the top right corner and click to close
changedFiles: plus eight further Win32 view pairs

frameworkVerified.evidence: the changed files are Avalonia .axaml views in the Windows head, OutputType>WinExe on net11.0-windows10.0.22621.0

selectedDefects.whySuitable: the close button of every custom-chrome Avalonia window has a hit region that does not reach the window's own corner, so a click at the corner falls through. The adapter reads the close button's bounding rectangle out of the UI Automation tree, clicks the corner point inside that rectangle, and asserts whether the window leaves the tree. That is precisely the geometry-plus-invoke path the Windows adapter has to get right for custom-chrome Avalonia windows, which are the common case for this framework
remaining: pick one window from the ten changed views and pin it as the subject
confirm the affected geometry is reported through UIA bounding rectangles rather than only in the Avalonia visual tree
build both revisions in the native x86_64 Windows VM

selectedDefects.issueTitle: Toggle folding should also toggle xml doc comments
selectedDefects.pullRequestTitle: Fix #749: toggle a member's fold together with its documentation

frameworkVerified.evidence: Avalonia, Avalonia.Desktop, Avalonia.Themes.Simple, Avalonia.AvaloniaEdit and AvaloniaEdit.TextMate package references, OutputType>WinExe on net10.0; no UseWPF

build.toolchain: .NET 10 SDK for the application; the test projects target net11.0

selectedDefects.whySuitable: an independent second application whose defect is in a hosted Avalonia editor control rather than in window chrome or raw input, so the two applications exercise different parts of the same adapter. The trigger clicks a folding margin in the AvaloniaEdit text view and the observable is the text the automation tree reports for the editor afterwards: on the affected revision the member folds while its documentation comment stays expanded
remaining: confirm AvaloniaEdit exposes its text through a UIA text or value pattern; if it does not, this candidate cannot be observed through the adapter and must be dropped
note that the report is filed as an enhancement rather than a bug, so the authority for the oracle is the project's own accepted behaviour change and not a platform rule
confirm the .NET 10 and .NET 11 SDKs required by the solution are installable in the guest
build both revisions in the native x86_64 Windows VM

selectedDefects.pullRequestTitle: Fix #781: click highlights member references, Ctrl+Click navigates

frameworkVerified.evidence: Avalonia, Avalonia.Desktop, Avalonia.Themes.Simple, Avalonia.AvaloniaEdit and AvaloniaEdit.TextMate package references, OutputType>WinExe on net10.0; no UseWPF

build.toolchain: .NET 10 SDK for the application; the test projects target net11.0

selectedDefects.whySuitable: the pointer semantics of a reference span change: a plain click must highlight the member's other references and only Ctrl+Click must navigate. The adapter drives it as a click at a computed point inside the Avalonia editor and observes whether the view navigated, which is visible as a change of the selected node in the tree view that the automation tree exposes next to the editor. It is a distinct identity from the folding candidate and touches the settings panel, so it also exercises a second Avalonia window
remaining: note that this defect's fixed revision is the previous candidate's affected revision, so the two must be built as separate checkouts
note that the report is filed as a long-standing enhancement request, so the oracle authority is an accepted behaviour change rather than a platform rule
decide the observable, preferring the tree view selection over editor highlight colour, which UIA will not report
build both revisions in the native x86_64 Windows VM

blockers.detail: no build, launch or UI Automation evidence exists for any candidate in this record. Every revision pair, framework classification and license here was verified from repository data on the host; nothing has been executed in the native x86_64 Windows VM

the Avalonia to Windows UI Automation bridge is assumed but unproven for these applications. Avalonia projects its own automation peers and exposes fewer of them than WPF, so for each candidate it is still unknown whether the observable is reachable through the automation tree at all. This is the single largest risk in this record and it applies to all five candidates
the toolchain is unusually new: ILSpy needs the .NET 10 SDK with net11.0 test projects and PicView needs the .NET 11 SDK. Neither has been confirmed installable in the Windows guest
